lesson_title: The Chip-Shop Test: Where Factories Choose to Live
hook_text: Why does the fish cannery live at the bay, but the cooldrink plant lives near you?
clip_script: Every industry type in the syllabus answers one everyday question: what is more of a pain to move — what the business uses, or what it sells? The chip shop stands at the taxi rank, not at the potato farm, because hot chips die in twenty minutes and hungry commuters will not travel for them. A fish cannery stands at St Helena Bay because fresh fish is a fast-spoiling, weight-losing raw material that shrinks into a light, long-lasting can — you ship the tin, never the fish. Fresh bread stales and cooldrink is mostly heavy glass, so the ovens and bottling lines sit in the cities. One question, and the factory always sits at the difficult end.
visual_style: Split-screen tug-of-war: fish trucks versus stacked cans, syrup drums versus crates of full bottles, with factories sliding along the rope to the heavier end.
pacing: Snappy question, two quick contrasts, satisfying rule at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson — five industry types, eight location factors, one test that sorts them all.
